issues.legal_issue: The statutory power to restrict or control exports includes the power to channel export trade through selected agencies and to limit which persons may participate.
material_facts: The governing statute authorized the government to prohibit, restrict, or otherwise control exports of specified goods.
An order made under that statute required licences for exporting specified goods and allowed licensing authorities to channel exports through special or specialised agencies or channels.
The government restricted manganese ore exports through quotas and selected groups of exporters, including a state trading corporation.
issues.conclusion: The statutory power encompassed channeling exports through selected agencies and classifying who could participate, so the relevant provision was within the authority conferred by the statute.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, 1947, authorizes control of exports that may include restrictions on the persons permitted to export and channeling trade through selected agencies. Clause 6(h) of the Export Control Order, 1958, was within that authority. The Court relied on Glass Chatons Importers and Users Association v. Union of India for the established validity of the canalising power. An agency may be “special” because it is selected to advance the purpose of channeling, and need not necessarily have prior expertise in that trade.

predicates.export_control_case: The case challenges a restriction or control imposed on the export of goods.
predicates.government_has_power_to_control_exports: The governing law authorizes the government to prohibit, restrict, or control exports.
predicates.trade_is_channelled_through_selected_age: The government directs exports of a commodity through agencies it has selected.

issues.definition: When an export-control case concerns a government authorized to control exports and trade channelled through selected agencies, the trade may be channelled through those agencies.

issues.legal_issue: The exclusion of new entrants from manganese ore exports and the preference given to a state trading corporation did not, in the circumstances, impose an unreasonable restriction on the right to carry on business.
material_facts: The internal market for manganese ore was negligible, and the ore was principally produced for export.
The export policy initially allocated quotas to established exporters and mineowners with export performance in specified years, as well as to the state trading corporation.
The appellant had no export performance in the specified years and was excluded from direct export participation.
The government selected the state trading corporation to help secure regular supplies of uniform quality, maintain continuity in foreign trade, and increase export earnings.
The appellant did not allege that established exporters or mineowners who received quotas had been improperly included in the eligible groups.
issues.conclusion: The majority held that the exclusion of newcomers and the selection of the state trading corporation were lawful restrictions in the circumstances and did not violate an enforceable right of the appellant.
issues.legal_principle: Article 19(1)(g) guarantees the right to carry on business, subject to reasonable restrictions in the interests of the general public under the first part of Article 19(6). The state-trade provision in Article 19(6)(ii) does not itself authorize a monopoly by administrative action; however, a restriction may still be valid under the general reasonable-restrictions provision. Where export control may lawfully take the form of channeling, excluding some groups is an inherent consequence. The government may classify participants according to the nature of the commodity and the circumstances of its export trade. The Court considered the need for regular supplies of uniform quality and continuity in trade, and found a rational basis for the selection made.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_export_restriction and negligible_domestic_market and export_policy_seeks_reliable_quality_and_supply and selected_agency_advances_export_objectives and newcomer_lacks_prior_export_experience and no_improper_inclusion_of_comparable_participants

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_export_restr: A person challenges an export restriction as an infringement of the right to carry on business.
predicates.negligible_domestic_market: There is little or no domestic market for the commodity, making export an important outlet for its producers.
predicates.export_policy_seeks_reliable_quality_and: The government adopts an export policy to secure regular supplies of consistent quality for foreign buyers.
predicates.selected_agency_advances_export_objectiv: The government selects an agency because it considers that agency likely to advance continuity of trade or export earnings.
predicates.newcomer_lacks_prior_export_experience: The excluded producer had no prior export performance in the period used to allocate participation or quotas.
predicates.no_improper_inclusion_of_comparable_part: The challenger does not establish that the participants who were included were improperly selected or comparable participants were unfairly treated.

issues.definition: If a business-rights challenge concerns an export restriction under these circumstances, the restriction is not unreasonable.

issues.legal_issue: The export-channeling policy was an unreasonable restriction when it left mineowners without a dependable outlet or safeguards for fair treatment.
material_facts: The domestic market for manganese ore was practically nonexistent.
Mineowners without prior export performance could not export directly and had to depend on established exporters or the state trading corporation to buy their ore.
Those buyers were not required to purchase a mineowner’s ore, and the mineowner could be left with no effective market or compelled to accept terms set by the available buyers.

The policy progressively reduced private quotas and later channelled exports through the state trading corporation without definite rules ensuring quotas, purchases, or fair prices for affected mineowners.
issues.conclusion: In his dissent, Subba Rao J. concluded that the policy infringed the appellant’s fundamental right by imposing an unreasonable restriction; he nevertheless considered the application for the expired licensing period infructuous and dismissed the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 19(1)(g), a restriction on business must satisfy the reasonable-restrictions standard in the first part of Article 19(6). Article 19(6)(ii) does not itself confer authority to create a monopoly by administrative action, though an administrative restriction may still be assessed under the general standard in Article 19(6). A scheme channeling exports should provide definite rules that protect affected producers through fair treatment and appropriate safeguards. Subba Rao J. referred to Saghir Ahmad v. State of U.P. in discussing the constitutional protection for restrictions on business.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_export_restriction and negligible_domestic_market and producers_cannot_export_directly and no_buyer_must_purchase_producers_goods and no_fair_treatment_safeguards

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_export_restr: A person challenges an export restriction as an infringement of the right to carry on business.
predicates.negligible_domestic_market: There is little or no domestic market for the commodity, making export an important outlet for its producers.
predicates.producers_cannot_export_directly: The policy prevents affected producers from exporting their goods themselves.
predicates.no_buyer_must_purchase_producers_goods: The available authorized buyers are not required to purchase the affected producers’ goods.
predicates.no_fair_treatment_safeguards: The scheme lacks definite safeguards for fair treatment, such as dependable allocation or fair pricing arrangements.

issues.definition: When an export restriction leaves producers without direct export access, a required buyer, or safeguards for fair treatment in a commodity with no meaningful domestic market, the restriction is unreasonable.
